messages:
Amanda Chen: FYI AcmeCorp is getting 429s overnight on our free tier during a scheduled demo run. They say it worked earlier in the week. They want a short-term uplift for a customer-facing demo tomorrow.

Amanda Chen: Quick summary from customer: heavy ingestion job (~18k requests over 2 hours), then steady traffic, now a 20% failure rate with 429s and some 500s. They pasted the response headers: `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 1865432520`.

acme_integration_bot: Automated webhook: job-id=ingest_2026-03-14-22, throughput=~2.5 r/s, peak=12 r/s, tokens=1.1M, auth=API key (free plan).

Amanda Chen: Repro steps customer provided:
1) curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACMEDEMO" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/complete
2) Observe "HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests" with body `{\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\"}` and headers above.

Samir Patel: Checking SRE console for that org... I see spikes around 02:10-03:00 UTC correlating with that job id. Free-tier limit for interactive endpoints is 60 requests/min and 200k tokens/day for this account (they've hit the token cap). The 500s are gateway timeouts from a downstream retry flood.

Amanda Chen: Customer insists it's a rate-limit config mismatch — they thought free tier was 150 rpm. They have screenshots from their dashboard showing "requests allowed: 150" (attached). Can someone verify UI vs enforcement?

Julia Kim: Billing view sometimes shows burst allowance in UI, but enforcement is based on backend quota. It can look inconsistent if cached. I can refresh the quota record for org acme-corp-22.

deploy-bot: quota-refresh job completed for org=acme-corp-22, change-log: none, source=cache-eviction, ts=1865432140.

Samir Patel: Confirmed backend shows 60 rpm / 200k tokens/day active. The UI screenshot must be stale or from a marketing page that lists default tiers.

Marcus Rivera: (Sales) If they want a short demo uplift we can offer a temporary 48h promo bump to 250 rpm and +1M token allotment, sales approval required. Need customer consent to upgrade billing contact or accept a 30-day invoice hold.

Amanda Chen: Customer asks: can we do the bump without a paid upgrade? They just need a demo for a potential large contract. Also they asked for a whitelist of our demo IPs in case they hit API key limits.

Samir Patel: We can do a scoped temp exception for 48h. Process: engineering-runbook -> support creates ticket with org and justification, SRE runs `support/grant-temp-quota --org acme-corp-22 --rpm 250 --tokens 1200000 --duration 48h --initiator support:AmandaC`. After that monitor for cascading retries.

Amanda Chen: Can you run that, Samir? I'll get the customer's billing contact on a quick approval.

Samir Patel: Running now. Output:
```
$ support/grant-temp-quota --org acme-corp-22 --rpm 250 --tokens 1200000 --duration 48h --initiator support:AmandaC
Request accepted. ticket=SUP-20482. effective_at=1865432170. expires_at=1865594970
```

ops-bot: Policy audit log appended: actor=Samir Patel, action=grant/temp_quota, org=acme-corp-22, rpm=250, tokens=1200000, ttl=48h, reason='demo uplift, sales/engineering signoff'.

Amanda Chen: Sent confirmation to customer, they started a new run and reported no 429s after 10 minutes. Will monitor and follow up if any 500s persist.

Julia Kim: Billing note: since this is a temporary, non-billable uplift, mark SUP-20482 with tag `promo-demo` and include sales contact Marcus Rivera for potential upsell.

Marcus Rivera: I'll follow up with the customer tomorrow. If they want longer term higher capacity, propose a Dedicated reserved slot or a paid plan at 1M tokens/day.

Samir Patel: One postmortem action: reconcile UI wording so free-tier marketing doesn't imply a burst cushion for enforcement. Filed ENG-5443.

Amanda Chen: Thanks everyone. Closing loop once the 48h window ends and customer confirms success. :thumbsup:
